newsitem.title: JAPAN: Konica sees Kodak deal lifting sales by 12 bln yen.
newsitem.headline: Konica sees Kodak deal lifting sales by 12 bln yen.

text.p: Konica Corp said on Wednesday it had agreed to supply digital copiers to Eastman Kodak Co and it expected the move to help boost sales.
"The agreement is expected to increase annual sales of our overseas copier business by 12 billion to 13 billion yen from some 60 billion yen currently," a Konica spokeswoman said.
She said it would help boost Konica's overall parent sales.
Konica, which makes photographic film and data processing equipment, is to supply high-speed digital copiers to Kodak which will be sold outside of Japan under the Kodak brand name, she said.
The digital copiers can be used as laser printers and can also process and edit images when connected to personal computers, the Konica spokeswoman said.
Konica expects to ship 10,000 units from Japan in the initial year, she said.
She declined to comment on the size of shipments in subsequent years.
In May, Konica said it expected parent sales of 390 billion yen for the year to March 31, 1998, up from 382.67 billion yen 1996/97.
